settingText: Present-day Vael-Tor arrival concourse: crowded, wet, ordinary, built over older foundations nobody thinks about anymore.
summary: Theo, Rae and Adrian arrive at Vael-Tor following a place-name recovered from the Desert Marker memories. The world feels stubbornly normal until Rae recognizes a structural shape from a memory she has never had before.

dialogueInline.text: You said that like you were apologizing.
I know where that corridor goes.
That hasn't worked for either of us yet.

directionInline.text: Open on ordinary civilian movement, vendors, luggage, rain on glass, transit announcements. The remembered shape should be subtle enough that Rae's recognition feels private before anything impossible occurs.

settingText: Vael-Tor public archive overlooking the transit platforms, with current maps layered over much older stonework.
summary: Rae finds an old city image beneath the current map. The name Atlas surfaces with it. Theo recognizes the name but not the memory, proving that their remembered histories continue to overlap without matching.

directionInline.text: An old image simply becomes legible beneath the present one: same place, different city. The name Atlas arrives as recognition, not metadata.

settingText: Vael-Tor observation gallery above a busy arrival field as a damaged refugee transport approaches.
summary: A refugee transport requests emergency landing while Vael-Tor's dormant defenses begin treating it as an enemy. Adrian recognizes the old defensive behavior and urges evacuation instead of investigation.

dialogueInline.text: You know what this place used to be.
There are people on that ship.
Then help them. Leave the history alone.

directionInline.text: Keep the crisis legible through human behavior: port workers stop, families look up, the refugee ship is visibly damaged. The ancient defense is frightening because present people do not know why their own city has decided those refugees are enemies.

settingText: Ancient memory: a populated world under catastrophic strain, streets buckling while civilians move beneath a failing sky.
summary: Rae's contact with the old wall opens a memory of Atlas holding a threatened world together while Starbreaker argues that preserving it will widen the war. Atlas refuses to turn the population into an acceptable loss.

dialogueInline.text: You can't hold a world forever.
I only need to hold it while people are still on it.
And when saving them carries this into the next system?
Then we save that one too.
It's the only one I can live with.

directionInline.text: He should feel burdened and physically committed, not triumphant. Starbreaker is recurring and should not be framed as cruel; he is asking about downstream cost. End before the memory tells us whether Atlas's choice made things better or worse.

settingText: Present-day Vael-Tor service corridor leading toward the old landing controls, crowded with frightened workers and improvised evacuation traffic.
summary: Rae comes out of the Atlas memory as the refugee ship is still descending. She chooses to help current workers open a path instead of chasing the memory for answers. Theo follows, irritated that this is exactly what Atlas would have done.

dialogueInline.text: You don't even know if the ship can land.

directionInline.text: The point is not that Rae is possessed by Atlas. She has simply seen a moral choice and is making her own. Keep her irritated by Theo's comparison because neither of them yet understands why the memory feels intimate.

settingText: Present-day maintenance access beneath Vael-Tor, old stone and current utility work built directly into one another.
summary: Theo follows the Marker fragment toward a sealed lower level and finds Adrian already trying to stop him. Adrian admits Vael-Tor was built over something the Reset did not remove.

directionInline.text: Theo follows recognition and physical architecture. Adrian says 'warship' because concealment is now more dangerous than the word.

settingText: Present-day exterior approach to Vael-Tor landing field during hard rain and emergency evacuation.
summary: Rae joins port workers manually clearing the approach while the old defenses keep threatening the refugee transport. She rejects an official suggestion to sacrifice the damaged ship to protect the station.

dialogueInline.text: You don't get to make them debris because that is easier to manage.

directionInline.text: Rae is not an engineer solving a control system. She works with people: opening gates, moving vehicles, getting families away from the landing zone, convincing someone with authority not to fire. Her choice rhymes with Atlas without becoming a reenactment.

settingText: Present-day Vael-Tor lower foundation chamber, where ordinary construction gives way to the curved black surface of something impossibly large.
summary: Theo and Adrian reach the buried hull. Theo understands that the city has literally been living on top of forgotten war matter. Adrian admits the Reset erased meaning, not mass.

dialogueInline.text: How long has this been here?
Who built their life on top of it.

directionInline.text: Let the hull reveal be architectural and quiet. Pipes, foundations and apartment supports have been attached to it over generations of apparent history. The horror is coexistence with forgotten matter, not activation effects.

settingText: Present-day Vael-Tor arrival field as the refugee transport attempts a dangerous landing among ordinary civilian infrastructure.
summary: Rae's effort gives the refugee transport a path to the ground. Theo returns from below as the city begins physically shifting around the buried ship.

dialogueInline.text: There's a ship under the city.
That was less surprising than I wanted.

directionInline.text: Use a small breath of exhausted humor. The refugee ship lands hard but survivably. The present-day human problem gets completed before the ancient spectacle takes over.

settingText: Present-day Vael-Tor foundations and skyline as the buried ancient dreadnought becomes visible beneath cracking modern structures.
summary: The ancient dreadnought emerges far enough to become undeniable public reality. The city does not transform into a battle zone; people simply see that their homes and streets were built across a history nobody remembered.

dialogueInline.text: You won't think that for long.

directionInline.text: The ship does not awaken as a machine. Earth and construction fall away, revealing more and more hull until denial is impossible. Let ordinary residents watching from balconies carry the scale.

settingText: Present-day landing field after the refugee transport is down, with passengers emerging into rain while the exposed dreadnought looms beyond.
summary: Rae and Theo watch living passengers emerge from the refugee ship. The immediate rescue matters more than the ancient object behind them. Theo begins to understand why Atlas's memory stayed with Rae.

dialogueInline.text: You had to ruin that sentence.
I had to tell the truth.

directionInline.text: Keep the camera emotionally with the refugees rather than the dreadnought. Atlas's theme lands through present people surviving, not through cosmic imagery.

settingText: Present-day Vael-Tor overlook at night, the exposed ancient dreadnought incorporated impossibly into the modern city below.
summary: Theo asks Adrian how something this large could survive while its history vanished. Adrian gives the series' material rule: forgetting removed the history, not the thing. Theo and Rae realize the present world may be built everywhere on forgotten consequences.

dialogueInline.text: And you thought that was enough.

directionInline.text: End quietly. The exposed dreadnought is now part of a living city. Adrian's admission should feel personal and shameful.
